text.content: Individual validation is not the same as end-to-end validation. Testing each fix in isolation confirms that the specific failure mode is resolved. It does not confirm that the fixes work correctly together, that one fix has not introduced a regression in another capability, or that the full execution path from consultant query to formatted response is intact across every path in the canvas.

text.content: End-to-end testing is the difference between a canvas that has been configured and a canvas that has been verified. Individual node tests confirm that each component works in isolation. An end-to-end test confirms that they work together. For example, routing decisions are correct, context transfers between nodes as expected, that failure paths exit cleanly, and that the agent's boundaries hold under realistic query conditions. This is the validation that gives a stakeholder confidence that the demonstration they are about to see reflects a system that actually works.
